chapter: Metronome, Billie Holiday, Cleveland and Atlantic
title: Playing with Billie Holiday and knowing her in Washington
summary: Billie was booked where he played; he had met her in Washington before she was famous.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: You made some recordings with Billie Holiday around that time also.
Yeah. Somehow, where we were playing at, she was booked in there, so. She
liked the way we played, so...
Yeah. Several clubs, I think Spotlite was one. And maybe the Famous Door, or Downbeat, one of 'em, I don't know.
Yeah, I played with her quite a bit.... I had known her before in Washington, when I was playing piano, I had met her before, yeah. That was before she was Billie Holiday. She was just starting out.
What was she doing in Washington?
I think she was livin' there. Maybe she was workin' there. But she hadn't become the star yet.
Did you know her as a singer?

Yeah, I believe she was livin' in Washington, I think. I know I was livin' there and I saw her several times -- quite a few times. But --- I wasn't playin' no guitar then. And when she found that I was playing guitar she was elated, like. And she heard the little band and said, "Yeah, keep that band." You know she worked long
with us. And we worked together a long time, And lots of times.
Did you work with her in Washington?

No, not with her. Just playin' piano with this little group we had. It was funny, we got a dollar a night and a sandwich, and this was at the airport in Virginia, that's exactly what we got, and we had to get there; so, some fella used to take us there. But that's all we got. $7 a week and a sandwich a night. We could live, that's funny.
